summary: Stevens County lookout 4 mi west of Northport. 1935 L-4 tower; DNR 40-ft tower 1971; removed 2013 for cell towers; cab now in Northport's town park.

facts.design: L-4 cab on a 40-foot timber tower (DNR tower built 1971); earlier 1935 L-4 tower and 1952 pole tower
facts.status_note: Tower dismantled in 2013. The cab was moved to Northport and sits in the town park. The lookout was removed to make way for a communication site (WillhiteWeb).

staffing.status: staffed every summer into the 2000s (firelookout.com); no longer staffed

access.note: The cab is in Northport's town park (2013 chapter report). WillhiteWeb reports a gate and says a walk is needed to reach the site. No source read says whether the summit is open to visitors.

visit.trail_note: WillhiteWeb reports a gate and says a walk is needed to reach the old site. The author has not visited.

events.note: Colville Examiner reported spur lines to Flagstaff Mountain and other peaks, to reduce the time to find fires
First tower: 40-foot L-4 tower with an L-4 cab; WillhiteWeb says the date is only reported and the tower was probably built a few years later
Pole tower with an L-4 cab. FFLOS and firelookout.com say 40 feet; WillhiteWeb says 50 feet
Known lookout personnel: Frank Kjolseth and Leon Hammer (firelookout.com)
Air Force acquired more than 50 acres by lease, with a county road license, for a radar station
Gap-filler radar station completed on the summit
Air Force deactivated the radar station in September and declared it excess in October
Removal of the Air Force improvements was contracted in September
DNR 40-foot timber tower with a live-in DNR cab
Tower taken down to make way for cell towers or a communication site; dismantled
Cab moved to the town of Northport; the 2013 chapter report says Northport adopted it and put it in a town park

corrections.why: The 1971 tower that stood until 2013 was 40 feet (about 12.2 m) per FFLOS and firelookout.com. 15.2 m is 50 feet, which matches only the 1952 tower in WillhiteWeb.

corrections.current: 2011 abandoned (to make way for cell towers)
corrections.proposed: remove the 2011 event; the documented removal is 2013
corrections.why: None of the pages I read gives 2011. The 2013 chapter report, WillhiteWeb and Weebly all date the removal to 2013.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: FFLOS, firelookout.com and the register give 1935 as the first tower date. WillhiteWeb says the 1935 date is only reported and the tower was probably built a few years later.

FFLOS and firelookout.com say the 1952 pole tower was 40 feet. WillhiteWeb says 50 feet, and the Weebly page also quotes a 50-foot tower. The 1971 tower that stood until 2013 was 40 feet in every source.
The register gives 4,187 ft (1,276 m). FFLOS and firelookout.com give 4,255 ft (1,297 m). The record's 1276.2 m follows the register.

notes_for_editor: The move to Northport and the 2013 removal are well supported by four sources. The 1935 start date, the 1952 tower height and the summit's current state are the weak points. The brief's 2011 abandonment event is not in any page read. The brief's 'None relocated' event is a garbled entry and was ignored. The brief's source list points to a sister record, us-wa-flagstaff-at-northport, which I did not read. The 1958-1961 Air Force radar station is in WillhiteWeb and Weebly but not in the register, FFLOS or firelookout.com. Access to the cab in the town park is inferred from its park location; no source says whether it can be entered. Reads used: 6 (register, FFLOS, 2013 PDF, firelookout.com, Weebly, WillhiteWeb).
